subject: Proposed localized-retain/handback language + certification timeline
body:
-- Message 1 --
From: Alicia Gomez <legal@acme-retail.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Reed <procurement@acme-retail.com>, Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on proposed retention carveouts and proof of deletion

Ben —

Thanks for sending over the draft DPA redlines. We reviewed the retention/deletion sections and have a few asks before we can proceed to procurement. High-level items:

- We need an explicit onshore copy-handback clause for US customer data (Section 7.2) — specifically: if we request local handback, what exact artifacts are delivered and what timeframe is Redwood committing to?
- Backup and snapshot TTLs: your draft allows a 90-day backup retention window; we have a 30-day requirement for our production PII. Can you confirm whether an exception is possible for named Acme Customer data?
- Proof of deletion: what is the format and scope of the deletion certificate? Will it include checksums, job IDs, and affected resource identifiers?

Attaching our retention matrix and a marked-up DPA excerpt. Can your security or legal team propose precise clause language for these three items? We want to avoid hand-wavy responses in the contract.

Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Senior Counsel, Acme Retail
[Attachment: Retention_matrix_ACME.xlsx (xlsx, 14KB)]
[Attachment: DPA_Acme_redlines_v3.docx (docx, 34KB)]

-- Message 2 --
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Alicia Gomez <legal@acme-retail.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 04 Jan 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on proposed retention carveouts and proof of deletion

Alicia —

Appreciate the clear ask and the matrix. I looped in Laura (Contracts) and Neha (Security/Compliance). Short answers first, then proposed clause text below for the DPA.

1) Onshore handback artifacts and timeline
- We can provide a localized handback package consisting of: (a) export of customer-controlled objects (user-provided data items referenced by tenant id), (b) snapshot handles for persistent storage, and (c) any associated audit logs relevant to the deletion window.
- Standard timeline: 30 days after a validated handback request. We can compress to 15 business days for customers on Dedicated or with an explicit professional services add-on.

2) Backup TTL for named customers
- By default our backup snapshot retention is 90 days. For named Acme accounts we can offer a contractual carveout to 30 days for production PII. This requires an operational change (segregated TTL tag on snapshots) and a 60-day lead time for automation rollout.

3) Proof of deletion format
- We provide a Deletion Certificate: CSV with resource ids, deletion timestamps, job IDs, and SHA256 of a manifest file; and a signed statement from our Compliance team. We can include the checksum manifest and a job run log.

Draft clause proposals (suggested insertions for Section 7.x):
- Localized Handback: "Upon Customer request, Redwood will export Customer Data in machine-readable format and deliver an operational package (data export, snapshot references, and applicable audit logs) within thirty (30) calendar days. For Dedicated deployments or for an agreed professional services engagement, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to deliver within fifteen (15) business days."

- Backup TTL Carveout: "Notwithstanding Section X, Redwood shall apply a retention TTL of thirty (30) calendar days to backups and snapshots containing Customer's Production PII where Customer is identified in the Contract as a 'Named Retention Carveout' customer. Customer acknowledges Redwood requires up to sixty (60) calendar days' notice to modify snapshot retention automation."

- Deletion Certificate: "Upon deletion of Customer Data, Redwood will provide a signed Deletion Certificate in CSV format listing resource identifiers, deletion timestamps, job identifiers, and SHA256 checksums of the manifest. Redwood will retain internal run logs for thirty (30) days and make them available for audit upon Customer request for thirty (30) days following deletion."

I've attached a redlined DPA with these language suggestions. Please let us know which of the three items are must-haves vs. negotiable.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: DPA_Acme_redlines_v3.docx (docx, 34KB)]

-- Message 3 --
From: Tom Reed <procurement@acme-retail.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Alicia Gomez <legal@acme-retail.com>, Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jan 2028 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on proposed retention carveouts and proof of deletion

Ben —

Thanks for the quick reply. Two clarifying items from procurement:
- Cost impact: if you implement the 30-day TTL carveout, will there be an ongoing surcharge or is this included in the standard deal?
- Operational SLA for handback: specify whether the 30-day (or 15 business day) timeline is a contractual SLA (with remedies) or a best-effort commitment.

If you can mark the clause language accordingly, procurement can sign off and move to DocuSign.

Tom
Tom Reed
Director, Procurement — Acme Retail

-- Message 4 --
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Tom Reed <procurement@acme-retail.com>, Alicia Gomez <legal@acme-retail.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 08 Jan 2028 09:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on proposed retention carveouts and proof of deletion

Tom/Alicia —

Couple points from Contracts & Security:

- Cost: The operational change to tag snapshots and maintain a carveout TTL is an engineering/ops change with a one-time implementation cost. Redwood will absorb the initial implementation cost for strategic pilot customers; ongoing incremental storage delta will be listed as an addendum to the pricing exhibit (we can provide a monthly per-GB rate). We suggest offering the 30-day carveout as an optional, billable add-on (with a credit for the first three months).

- SLA vs Best-effort: Redwood is comfortable making the 30-calendar-day handback a contractual obligation. The 15-business-day expedited timeline should be a binding SLA only for Dedicated customers or customers that have committed to a professional services engagement; otherwise it is a "commercially reasonable efforts" commitment. Remedies for SLA misses: service credit up to 5% of monthly committed fee for each missed SLA occurrence, capped at 25% for the month.

- Proof-of-deletion scope: Security requests that manifest-level checksums are included and that any proof includes the job ID, the storage path namespace, and a signed statement. We will redact internal operational IDs not relevant to the customer. Redwood will preserve deletion artifacts for 90 days to support dispute resolution.

Proposed edit to procurement + legal: we will include the following as contract language and provide a pricing addendum. If Acme agrees, we will get DocuSign-ready redlines by Thu, Jan 11.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

-- Message 5 --
From: Alicia Gomez <legal@acme-retail.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Reed <procurement@acme-retail.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jan 2028 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on proposed retention carveouts and proof of deletion

Laura —

Thanks for the transparency. A couple of follow-ups from legal:
- We need the handback SLA to be symmetric: if Redwood requires more than 30 days for your operational reasons, Acme must have the right to request a one-time export extension and Redwood must notify us and provide an estimated completion date.
- The deletion artifacts need to include tenant-level identifiers (PVC/tenant id) and scoped storage paths. The 90-day retention for debug artifacts is acceptable, but we require that Redwood commit to preserving those artifacts for the full 90 days in an immutable archive for the purpose of audits.
- Regarding pricing: Acme prefers predictable fee language. Please provide a concrete monthly per-GB number and an example calculation for a 30 TB production dataset.

If you can get the redline and pricing addendum to us by Jan 11 we can proceed to sign-off.

Alicia

-- Message 6 --
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Alicia Gomez <legal@acme-retail.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on proposed retention carveouts and proof of deletion

Alicia/Tom —

Operational notes from Security & Ops: practical implications and a recommended implementation plan if Acme signs the carveout:

1) Implementation steps (timeline estimate):
- Week 0–2: Contract sign-off and SLA/manifest format finalization.
- Week 3–8: Engineering implementation: add TTL tagging, update snapshot lifecycle jobs, ensure manifest generation pipeline includes resource ids and checksums.
- Week 9–12: QA and separation testing in staging.
- Week 13: Rollout to production tenant(s).

2) Handback export contents (minimum deliverables):
- Full export of customer-supplied objects (NDJSON / compressed tar),
- Snapshot references and the manifest CSV (resource id, path, deletion timestamp, job id, SHA256),
- Audit log slice for the retention window (iso8601 timestamps),
- Signed Deletion Certificate (PDF).

3) Immutable retention for debug artifacts: Ops will write deletion manifests to a WORM-configured bucket (90-day retention) and produce an audit hash chain for verification.

4) Pricing example: For a 30 TB dataset with the carveout enabled: monthly incremental storage delta estimated at $0.03/GB/month -> $900/month. First three months credit applies as discussed.

If Acme confirms acceptance of the above and authorizes Redwood to proceed with tagging, we will queue the implementation and provide a test export in staging within 10 weeks.

Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference

[End of thread]
